Use case: ads-marketing. Create exactly one finished single flat opaque landscape 16:9 SNS poster for a weekend houseplant market. 요청한 화면 비율을 유지하면서 현재 도구와 모델이 지원하는 가능한 최대 해상도로 출력.

Input image 1 is a newly authored planning guide for copy anatomy, readable text areas and the relationship of a substantial plant drawing to the reading axis. Its shapes are temporary planning marks; create the finished botanical drawing described here. Coordinates, line count and font sizes are flexible planning choices, not preservation conditions.

Visual design: an observant, sensuous contemporary botanical editorial poster. On a cool pale pink ground, draw one substantial living houseplant occupying the left almost-half, from richly observed leaves down through a cutaway pot to connected branching roots. Use precise dark plum botanical pen contours and fine veins, with translucent plum, lavender and muted rose washes. Several large leaves turn in different directions, some face-on with branching veins, another subtly folded to show the underside. Their petioles join a coherent branching stem which enters the soil and continues as a root crown and believable finer roots in the cutaway. Keep leaf edges crisp and fine; use restrained crosshatching only where form needs it. The pot is warm muted rose, its cutaway exposes an earthy translucent soil section containing connected, tapering, naturally branching roots. A grown human hand enters from the left with wrist and fingers clearly joined, gently attending and touching the pot rim; make the contact unambiguous. A soft plum ground wash anchors the pot and hand without a hard rectangular field. This is a clean observational image device for understanding attentive care, with no labels or technical promises. The image must carry the joy of choosing and getting to know a living plant, not ornamental edge foliage, toy modelling or a tiny decoration.

Composition and typography: let the leaf canopy be the left visual entry and the broad Korean main Title be the immediately recognizable typographic anchor on the right. Its deep plum, mature contrast-stroke Korean serif anatomy has confident broad proportions, clear counters, compatible syllable rhythm and breathing space. Keep the market line as a subordinate eyebrow above it, the English name as a smaller companion just below it, then the short sentence as a clear medium-weight Subtitle. Place the whole explanatory paragraph below in mature regular Korean serif text with stable starts, natural word spaces, moderate leading and meaning-led soft wraps. Allow four or five readable lines rather than squeezed tiny type. Plan for comfortable reading at a 720-pixel-wide display; body and useful footer letters need sufficient optical size and contrast. A short gap after the paragraph leads directly to larger regular date/hour serif numerals, then the place, followed by nearby access/care and invitation/URL groups on the same optical left axis. Footer sans supports the serif voice with compatible widths, baselines and optical size. Keep clean digits, colons, middle dots and the original en-dashes as distinct long midline bars. Let generous leaves and fine root structures balance the text's varying line lengths across the whole image. All typography belongs to the native finished image; render precise, smooth letter edges independent of the drawing wash.

Print exactly the following twelve entries, each once, with original Korean/Latin letters, meaningful word spaces, numbers and punctuation. Soft line wrapping at word boundaries is allowed. This list contains all printable text:

Finish and constraints: clean opaque full-bleed image with deliberate contour-to-wash depth, smooth cool pink ground and controlled local hatching. No antique labels, distressed paper, decorative seal, scientific labels, species names, measurements, invented facts, extra print, logo, QR, watermark, mockup, frames, comparison panels or contact sheet.
